| Actor | Primary need |
| --- | --- |
| Developer | Checks and corrects a local working tree; explores architecture; traces affected features and tests; debugs by subsystem and feature stage. |
| Rule author | Defines normative specifications, applicability requirements, mechanical checks, correction effects, examples, evaluations, and agent guidance. |
| Language-package author | Integrates syntax, semantics, compilers, linters, formatters, refactorings, debugging, and project models behind capability contracts. |
| Repository architect | Declares layers and subsystem constraints; compares declared and inferred architecture; reviews boundary leakage, cycles, and feature scattering. |
| Team lead/reviewer | Reviews gates, policy changes, baselines, suppressions, agent plans, architecture changes, and historical trends. |
| CI/release operator | Runs reproducible gates, retains snapshots and attestations, controls waivers, and blocks regressions. |
| Agent orchestrator | Consumes typed task envelopes, invokes only approved capabilities, returns structured work results, and repairs validated findings. |
| Platform administrator | Configures plugins, workers, models, sandboxing, caches, access policies, organization rules, and hosted/self-hosted deployment. |
| Mobile reviewer | Receives alerts, triages blocking findings, reviews evidence, and approves or rejects bounded remote actions. |
| External tool builder | Queries symbols, edges, metrics, findings, snapshots, topology, and diffs through APIs without depending on Nomos UI internals. |

| Model | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| WorkspaceContext | Repository, branch/commit/working tree, configuration, installed packages, toolchain, snapshot, trust context. |
| Artifact and Symbol | Stable language-neutral identities for repositories, projects, packages, modules, files, types, functions, blocks, expressions, schemas, services, generated artifacts, and runtime symbols. |
| RelationshipEdge | Containment, dependency, call, dataflow, mutation, message, implementation, generation, co-change, ownership, runtime communication, feature membership, evidence relation. |
| Capability | Named operation or fact with guarantees, quality rank, granularity, provider, and compatibility metadata. |
| Rule and Applicability | Normative contract, requirements, configuration, effective support state, reason, coverage, and phase/gate membership. |
| Finding | Rule, subject/geometry, evidence, severity, confidence, applicability, coverage, provenance, fixes, suppressibility, and lifecycle. |
| FindingGeometry | Renderer-neutral spatial or relational extent of a finding. Canonical forms are PointGeometry, RegionGeometry, EdgeGeometry, CycleGeometry, ClusterGeometry, and FieldGeometry. It references canonical subjects, graph nodes or edges, source ranges, grouping relations, and evidence; it does not define rendering coordinates. |
| FindingVisualizationProjection | Optional RulePackage presentation projection containing FindingGeometry, grouping hints, scalar overlays, comparison identity, explanation layers, and predicted transformation geometry. It may enrich rendering and interaction but shall not alter the normative Finding. |
| MetricObservation | Metric ID, subject, value/unit, scope, build/capture ID, provider, configuration, confidence, coverage, evidence. |
| MetricTradeoffProjection | Renderer-neutral comparison of current, historical, or predicted alternatives across a declared set of MetricDescriptors. It preserves original and normalized values, directionality, uncertainty, evidence classification, baseline, optional weighting, dominance relations, and missing dimensions; it does not declare a universally best alternative or define rendering geometry. |
| Subsystem and Architecture | Declared/inferred subsystem, layer, boundary ports, constraints, candidate membership, confidence, lenses, comparison outcome. |
| Feature and Scenario | Product feature, entry points, roles, intended/static/observed topology, scenarios, boundaries, inputs, outputs, confidence, evidence. |
| FeatureTestContract | Preconditions, inputs, required path obligations, integration crossings, outputs, forbidden effects, allowed alternatives, evidence requirements. |
| DebugSession | Target, thread, frame, stop reason, source/symbol mapping, architecture breadcrumb, feature role/stage, execution trail, semantic breakpoints. |
| Gate, Phase, Workflow | Typed DAG of scopes, providers, rules, tests, agents, approvals, conditions, artifacts, failure behavior, caching, and execution history. |
| CorrectionPlan | Candidate operations, dependencies, effect contracts, conflicts, optimization objective, validation plan, transaction, state transitions, result. |
| Snapshot and Diff | Versioned source/config/provider identity, normalized graph/metrics/findings/coverage, identity transitions, historical comparison. |
| Evidence and Attestation | Raw/normalized evidence references, tool outputs, command/config hashes, environment identity, claims, signatures, and reproducibility metadata. |
| SelectionContext | Cross-client selection of artifacts, rules, subsystem, feature, scenario, findings, snapshot, baseline, lens, and debug session. |
| Canonical identity kernel | Artifact, Symbol, Resource, Subject, SnapshotEntity, identity transitions, confidence, and provenance. |
| BuildVariant | Target framework/platform, language/dialect version, feature flags, conditional symbols, environment, generation inputs, and provider configuration. |
| ProtocolBinding | Typed cross-language/service/schema binding with endpoints, contract version, direction, confidence, and evidence. |
| EvidenceClassification | Authoritative, Verified, Observed, Derived, Approximate, Predicted, AgentJudged, or HumanAsserted evidence and intended use. |
| WorkflowStepContract | Typed I/O, side effects, idempotency, retries, timeout, cache, privileges, cancellation, compensation, determinism, and emitted evidence. |
| TelemetryJunction and ExecutionTrace | Causally linked observations at every significant boundary, preserving timing, artifacts, status, resources, usage, cost evidence, failures, retries, cache behavior, provider identity, and policy treatment. |
| ModelBackendPackage | Neutral inference backend registration for hosted APIs, self-hosted endpoints, embedded runtimes, and local models, with model discovery, capability guarantees, authentication, usage/cost reporting, data-boundary metadata, and conformance. |
| AgentExecutorPackage | Adapter for coding-assistant chats, CLIs, IDE agents, human execution, subscription agents, or recorded replay over the common task/result protocol, with declared mutation, evidence, telemetry, and automation guarantees. |
| ModelUsageObservation and CostObservation | Provider-neutral token/unit, latency, tool-call, cache, retry, model, and monetary evidence with exact-versus-estimated status, accounting method, rate source, currency, and uncertainty. |

| Subsystem | Owned responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| Package Registry & Compatibility | Own package metadata, authenticated manifests, dependency/version resolution, signatures, registry sources, compatibility planning, and package-state description. It does not install tools, host provider processes, or own authoring SDK behavior. |
| Workspace & Project Discovery | Detect repository, project graph, languages, build systems, generated/vendor/test code, configuration, and trust boundaries. |
| Indexer & Identity Service | Incrementally parse/index source and artifacts; maintain stable IDs, source mappings, identity transitions, and dependency-aware invalidation. |
| Capability Registry & Composer | Match operation requirements to installed providers; rank strategies; report guarantees, fallbacks, and missing capabilities. |
| Applicability Engine | Compute rule × language × provider × repository configuration support and exact reason for every target combination. |
| Rule Engine | Evaluate deterministic rule packages over normalized facts; import native diagnostics; emit typed findings and coverage. |
| Gate/Workflow Engine | Execute typed DAGs with concurrency, prerequisites, caching, retries, approvals, artifacts, progress, and reproducibility. |
| Correction Planner | Generate candidate fixes, model interactions, choose compatible sets, stage transactions, validate, detect cycles, and roll back. |
| Rule Interaction Analyzer | Maintain declared/observed rule graph, conflict matrix, confluence tests, oscillation metrics, unsatisfiable subsets, and policy simulations. |
| Metrics & Observation Store | Normalize static, compiler, Git, binary, runtime, profiler, test, and Nomos metrics with descriptors and provenance. |
| Program Atlas Service | Build renderer-neutral hierarchies and overlays for source size, findings, metrics, history, binary output, runtime behavior, and diffs. |
| Architecture & Subsystem Engine | Model declared architecture, infer multiscale communities across lenses, identify boundaries/ports, cycles, layer skips, and topology differences. |
| Feature Topology Engine | Map features/scenarios to code, tests, runtime traces, inputs/outputs, boundaries, confidence, change impact, and historical evolution. |
| Test Intelligence Engine | Create test obligations, classify test paths, select tests for diffs, detect over-mocking/accidental integration, compare passing/failing traces. |
| Debug Projection Service | Consume DAP/IDE/runtime events and map frames/trails to symbols, subsystems, layers, features, tests, and semantic breakpoints. |
| Agent Safety & Policy Service | Build and validate task/result envelopes, partition permissions, enforce scope and threat controls, label judgment, record assumptions, and authorize read/propose/preview/mutate/execute/approve/publish classes. Executor hosting is separate. |
| Knowledge Integration Adapter | Query KnowledgeWorkbench for claims/decisions/provenance and emit Nomos findings/observations back through neutral contracts. |
| API/CLI/MCP/LSP Gateway | Expose the same application services through versioned structured interfaces, streaming, exports, and read/write separation. |
| Client State & Deep-Link Service | Preserve selections and exact queries across desktop, web, mobile, CLI, IDE, and shared links. |
| Security/Sandbox/Attestation | Authenticate, authorize, sandbox tools/agents, restrict network/filesystem, verify packages, enforce resource limits, and sign results. |
| Capability Contract Registry | Version capability semantics, guarantees, variants, schemas, failure/coverage behavior, and conformance suites. |
| Build Variant & Generation Service | Resolve configured program variants and generated-artifact lineage; redirect edits to authoritative sources. |
| Evidence Authority Service | Classify evidence, preserve disagreement, and apply explicit resolution policies without erasing provenance. |
| Workflow Transaction Manager | Persist step effects, idempotency tokens, cancellation/compensation state, recovery, and replay metadata. |
| Cross-Language Binding Resolver | Create typed bindings across FFI, RPC, schemas, generated clients, messages, databases, and runtime observations. |
| Integration Runtime & Environment Manager | Install and activate packages; discover external tools; host/sandbox provider processes; enforce permissions/resource limits; diagnose environment health; perform rollback. |
| Event & Notification Service | Publish typed events; manage subscriptions, in-product inbox, external delivery providers, approval tasks, acknowledgment, escalation, expiration, and deep-linked evidence. |
| Agent Executor Adapter Service | Host API-model, subscription-agent, human, and recorded-replay adapters over the common task/result protocol without owning safety policy. |
| Package SDK & Projection Toolchain | Scaffold packages; run fixtures/conformance; inspect mappings; generate and validate projections; package, sign, publish, deprecate, and report migrations. |

| Form | Minimum contents |
| --- | --- |
| PointGeometry | Exactly one primary canonical subject or one source position, with snapshot and evidence identity. |
| RegionGeometry | One or more source ranges or a bounded set of canonical graph nodes, with boundary and completeness semantics. |
| EdgeGeometry | A typed source endpoint, typed target endpoint, relationship identity, direction where meaningful, and supporting evidence. |
| CycleGeometry | A canonicalized ordered cycle of relationship edges, with optional containing strongly connected component identity. |
| ClusterGeometry | A member set, grouping relation or criterion, membership evidence, and an explicit overlap policy. |
| FieldGeometry | A declared domain, scalar or categorical values, value provenance, propagation basis where used, and direct-versus-derived classification. |

| Semantic change class | Baseline autonomy disposition | Authority / approval expectation | Minimum evidence and control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local implementation | Autonomous when explicitly in scope | Mutate authority under the active ChangeIntent; no separate owner approval unless policy requires it | Contract unchanged; focused compile/tests/checks; bounded rollback |
| Contract-compatible extension | Autonomous or preview-first by policy | Mutate authority; designated contract owner review when the compatibility claim is uncertain or public behavior expands | Compatibility evidence; existing-contract tests; affected-provider and variant validation |
| Public-interface change | Review required | API or contract owner approval before publication; mutation may be proposal-only | Consumer impact, migration and compatibility evidence, versioning treatment, rollback plan |
| Dependency-boundary change | Review required | Repository architect or dependency-boundary owner approval | Dependency graph delta, boundary rules, build variants, affected tests, reversal plan |
| Architecture-topology change | Autonomous execution prohibited by default | Repository architect or recorded architecture-decision authority | Architecture decision contract, counterfactual topology, alternatives, migration and rollback |
| Behavioral-default change | Review required | Product, subsystem, or policy owner approval | Default-selection rationale, compatibility, scenario and regression evidence, explicit rollout/rollback |
| Correctness or safety obligation change | Autonomous execution prohibited | Named correctness, safety, or risk-acceptance authority | Formal obligations, fault/negative tests, evidence sufficiency, independent approval and recovery |
| Policy or configuration change | Review required unless narrowly delegated | Policy owner or configuration authority | Effective-configuration diff, affected repositories/variants, precedence and rollback |
| Rule change | Autonomous publication prohibited | Rule owner and governed RulePackage promotion authority | Normative version impact, fixtures/evaluations, calibration evidence, migration and rollout |
| Generated-artifact change | Redirect or review according to lineage | Generator/source owner when output is not SafeToEdit; otherwise normal class-specific authority | Generated lineage, authoritative source, regeneration proof, no direct-edit drift |
| Destructive removal | Autonomous execution prohibited by default | Owner approval for the removed surface plus affected architecture/API/policy authorities | Usage and dependency proof, alternatives, migration/deprecation treatment, recoverability |

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Applicability | Whether a rule can and should run for a subject under current capabilities and configuration. |
| Architecture breakpoint | A semantic breakpoint such as entering a subsystem or crossing a layer, resolved to debugger breakpoints or instrumentation. |
| Atlas | Renderer-neutral hierarchical/graph model that overlays software structure with metrics, findings, coverage, history, and runtime evidence. |
| Capability | A provider-neutral fact or operation with stated guarantees. |
| Conformance fixpoint | A state where enabled correction strategies require no further changes under the selected policy. |
| Coverage | What subjects and facts were actually evaluated, excluded, unsupported, or failed. |
| Feature topology | Evidence-backed graph slice that realizes a user-visible capability across architecture, code, tests, and runtime. |
| Finding geometry | A renderer-neutral description of the spatial or relational extent of a finding. Canonical forms are point, region, edge, cycle, cluster, and field geometries. It references canonical subjects, graph nodes or edges, source ranges, grouping relations, and evidence without defining rendering coordinates. |
| Finding visualization projection | An optional RulePackage presentation projection containing finding geometry, grouping hints, scalar overlays, comparison identity, explanation layers, and predicted transformation geometry. It may not alter the normative finding. |
| Gate | Policy that decides whether an engineering state may proceed. |
| Language package | Independently versioned collection of language recognition, capabilities, provider strategies, and projections. |
| Phase | Execution configuration for a coherent set of tools/rules over a scope. |
| Provider | Implementation of a capability, such as Roslyn semantics, Clippy diagnostics, DAP debugging, or perf samples. |
| Rule package | Versioned normative specification, judgment, correction, evidence, docs, and evaluation unit. |
| Scenario contract | Inputs, preconditions, path obligations, outputs, allowed alternatives, and evidence required for one feature behavior. |
| Snapshot | Reproducible normalized state of a workspace at a source/config/provider identity. |
| Subsystem candidate | Explainable inferred community that may or may not match declared architecture. |
| Task envelope | Typed constraints and context presented to an agent or human executor. |
| Workflow | Typed orchestration of mechanical, agent, knowledge, test, approval, and artifact steps. |
| Artifact | A persisted or generated repository/build object such as a file, package, binary, schema, or configuration. |
| Subject | A canonical reference to an Artifact, Symbol, Resource, runtime entity, or typed aggregate evaluated by a rule, metric, policy, or test obligation. |
| SnapshotEntity | A versioned occurrence of a canonical entity under one repository/build/configuration snapshot. |
| Build variant | One configured semantic program defined by target, platform, feature flags, conditional symbols, generation inputs, and provider configuration. |
| Capability contract | A versioned definition of operation/fact semantics, schemas, guarantees, coverage, and failure behavior. |
| Package | A versioned installable unit containing registration, contracts, providers, rules, metadata, fixtures, or client integration. |
| Protocol binding | A typed, evidenced relationship connecting artifacts across languages, services, schemas, or generated interfaces. |
| Correction | A planned and auditable artifact transformation; preferred over the ambiguous terms fix or remediation in schemas. |
| Run | One execution instance of a check, gate, workflow, test, or analysis against pinned inputs. |
| Capture | A set of runtime observations collected during a defined interval or scenario. |
| Architecture layer | A declared system tier such as presentation, application, domain, or infrastructure. |
| Semantic zoom level | The aggregation depth used to project the same graph as subsystem, module, file, type, function, or block. |
